# An ordinary goal-directed baseline defeats the previous sufficient ledger

This is a **separate comparator**, not a replacement theorem or a new learning
algorithm. All earlier reviewed sources and archives remain unchanged. The
current finite-state example does not establish a consequential advantage of
our operator certificate. This comparator is goal-specific; it does not replace
the earlier uniform compatible-goal/operator certificate.

## 1. Task and actual information interface

The fixed public task is the pinned 4096-state, two-action, 24-step source,
initially uniform on its public initial support, with terminal reward the public
indicator b of G. Initial support is disjoint from G. Source access returns
sampled destination labels for named current labels/actions; block membership
is an acquired retained lookup. The learner is not given hidden groups, edge
lists, a useful decomposition, transition probabilities, or optimal values.
The same ordinary coarse-count community proposal acquires four blocks. All
pilot and incoming row-count batches used below were taken after that proposal.
The reused counts are exact recorded integers, not new observations. Direct
source implementation access appears only in the **source-side adapter audit**,
not in the planner or hazard estimator.

The deployed policy is an ordinary 24-by-4 action table with a 4096-entry block
lookup. It can run in an explicit-state simulator that returns the next label;
there is no claim of a physical sensor or hidden-state implementation. Each
step costs a source transition, label update, block lookup and policy lookup.

## 2. Confidence radius and fixed prefixes

For N iid Bernoulli trials and count c, put

    v(c)=c(N-c)/(N(N-1)),
    R(c,N,K)=min(1, sqrt_up(2 v(c) K/N) + 7K/[3(N-1)]).

`sqrt_up` is the retained exact dyadic upper square root with 40 fractional bits.
Maurer–Pontil (2009), Theorem 4, implies the one-sided upper/lower bounds at
failure probability zeta whenever K >= log(2/zeta). For two-sided receiving use
K >= log(4/zeta). We use K=(7/10) ceil(log2 x) >= ln x; ln 2 < 7/10 follows,
for example, from the positive Taylor lower sum for exp(7/10)>2.

Six possible acquisition prefixes are budgeted before data, though this saved
trace stops after the third. At prefix t the row half-batch size is 512*2^t,
with the fixed replicate count prescribed by the original confidence

# Ordinary goal-specific comparator — reviewed local checkpoint

The useful result is an ordinary baseline win, not a new learning algorithm:
fixed-goal max-hazard upper + fresh policy Monte Carlo gives regret
0.056432232574415674 (request 0.0565), with prospective 812,951,680 source calls.
All three acquisition/evaluation attempts are charged. The ordinary interval-
MDP candidate alone remains a recorded failure at approximately 0.069282921.
The previous 3.299-billion-call operator acquisition and norm work are not
refunded; they are not necessary lower bounds. The same retained information
is available to competitors. This is a small simulator fixture, not practical
or civilisation-level advantage.

## Review and scope
The whole source-bound receipt is
`two_rate_operator_acquisition_20261031/interval_mdp_comparator/reviewer_2047/INDEPENDENT_WHOLE_COMPARATOR_REVIEW.md`.
It binds the 28-entry frozen manifest. It covers full check_comparator.run,
not goal_hazard.py alone. The deterministic source argument-law transport,
fixed-goal scope, iid/fresh/nonanticipating sampling premises, external task
binding, failed attempts, finite-bit costs, and source-side audit are explicit.
The older retained-large receipt remains scoped to its own original sources;
not every dependency/file in this ZIP is newly independently reviewed.

## Reproduce (local, no downloads or installation required)
With existing Python, numpy and sympy, from extracted root:

    cd two_rate_operator_acquisition_20261031/interval_mdp_comparator
    python -c 'import check_comparator as c; print(c.run())'

This nonmutating replay performs 17,026 exact checks + 16 rejections and
regenerates all 18 million evaluation transitions. Main script entry points
may write their original output filenames; prefer run(). Reviewer extra checks
and exact replay outputs are retained separately, together with the receipt.

## Allowlist and exclusions
Only the original freeze allowlist, its manifest, four reviewer files and these
checkpoint metadata files are included. No caches, administrative/private files,
external credentials, unrelated branches or ongoing tagged/full-record/
population work are included. All originals and previous archives are unchanged.
This checkpoint was created locally only; no upload/publication/transfer.
SHA256SUMS covers every payload except itself; archive hash is in the external
sidec
